prompt: When someone posts, it should appear in all their followers' home timelines, which must load in under 100 ms.
why: Fan out on write: push the post ID into each follower's precomputed timeline.
trap: A queue may carry the work, but the design choice is precomputing each follower's feed.

prompt: Most users have 200 followers, but a few celebrities have 50 million. Writing every celebrity post into every follower's feed takes hours.
why: Hybrid fan-out: push for normal users, pull celebrity posts at read time and merge.
trap: More shards just spread the same 50 million writes around.

prompt: A project tool shows each user a feed of updates from the projects they follow, newest first.
why: Same shape as a social feed: fan updates out to followers' feeds.
trap: Push connections can deliver updates live, but you still need the stored feed.

prompt: 90% of followers never open the app, yet every post is written into all of their feeds.
tells: 90% of followers never open the app
written into all of their feeds
why: Switch inactive users to fan-out on read: build their feed only when they return.
trap: It's not a caching issue; it's choosing push vs pull per user.

prompt: When a group admin posts an announcement, all 80,000 group members should get a notification in their inbox.
why: Fan-out on write copies the item into each member's inbox (via a queue of jobs).
trap: Push delivers it live; fan-out decides who gets a copy.

prompt: For users following few accounts, building the feed by merging those accounts' recent posts at read time is cheap enough.
tells: merging those accounts' recent posts at read time
why: That's fan-out on read: no copies at write, merge when asked.
trap: It's the alternative strategy for the same feed problem.

prompt: Normal users' posts are pushed into followers' feeds, while celebrity posts are merged in when a follower opens the app.
tells: merged in when a follower opens the app
why: Hybrid fan-out: write for most, read for the heavy hitters.
trap: The combination is the classic Twitter-style answer.

prompt: A forum sends each subscriber a daily email listing new posts in the threads they follow.
tells: new posts in the threads they follow
why: Collect per-subscriber updates and deliver one per person: fan-out to followers.
trap: A queue moves the work; fan-out decides the recipients.
